localBiteReport: The most recent available report covering Choctawhatchee Bay specifically is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 — about two weeks old. That report (greatdaysoutdoors.com) describes the bay entering its early fall transition: large schools of baitfish (greenies/pogies) have pushed from open deeper water into bayous, flats, bridge areas, and rolldowns, drawing predators into more accessible positions. Capt. Blake Nelson (Last Cast Charters) noted bull redfish and jack crevalle actively feeding on those bait schools around Boggy Bayou, Rocky Bayou, Joe's Bayou, Marler Bayou, and near the East Pass. Slot-sized redfish were also moving up, and trout plus mangrove snapper were holding around grass edges, sandy pockets, and docks. Looking ahead from that report, the expectation was that the fall mullet run — and with it the first meaningful push of slot redfish — would arrive in the second or third week of September (right about now), making this a prime window to watch flats and drains carefully. Water temperature at this exact location today is 86°F.
